subject: Post-call recap: VirtuaSoft throughput & topology confirmation
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eleanor James <eleanor.james@virtuasoft.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: VirtuaSoft throughput & topology confirmation

Hi Eleanor —

Thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap from our side and the concrete asks we promised to follow up on.

High-level pain & goals we captured
- Current infra: VirtuaSoft runs a mix of short transactional prompts (chatbots, search augmentation) and longer-context generation (doc summarization). Major pain is tail latency spikes during peak traffic windows and ballooning token cost when queries hit the 8–12k token range.
- Goal: 95p latency < 300ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens); stable p95 cost per 1k tokens under your target for chat use-cases; predictable autoscaling for daily traffic bursts.

Technical constraints you mentioned
- Must keep customer PII within VPC (private deployment for production).
- Prefer dedicated GPU pools for peak windows, with fast fallback to hosted variants in region.
- Primary model family target: Llama-2 style 70B chat variant or equivalent open model with similar throughput/quality tradeoffs. Quantization acceptable if we preserve safety/quality.

Initial topology sketch (from call)
- Staging/POC: single-region dedicated cluster (4x A100-80GB equiv) behind Redwood routing; continuous batching for short calls; prefix KV cache to handle repeated retrievals.
- Prod: multi-pool approach — reserved pod for steady baseline (predictable throughput), autoscale pool for bursts, and a lower-cost fallback pool (quantized 16-bit or 8-bit model) for best-effort requests during overload.

SLOs we discussed (provisional)
- Latency: 95th percentile ≤ 300ms (short prompts, <=512 tokens), 99th percentile < 800ms with appropriate autoscale headroom.
- Throughput: steady-state 400 rps for the core service, bursting to 1,200 rps with autoscale.
- Availability: 99.9% region-level for dedicated setup (SLA to be finalized).

Deliverables attached/in-flight
- virtuaSoft-slo-draft.pdf (attached): initial SLO table and proposed measurement points.
- topology-diagram.vsdx (attached): rough cluster + routing diagram.

Open asks / next steps (we promised to 1)–3))
1) Can you confirm a realistic 1-week peak (rps) and an example short prompt payload size (avg tokens) so we can size KV cache and batching defaults?
2) Please share the security evidence contact (SOC2 owner) so we can surface the right compliance artifacts; we’ll include a limited-scope architecture whitepaper for your security team.
3) We propose a technical deep-dive next Tue or Wed (60m) where our infra engineer (Connor) will walk the topology and run a quick throughput baseline plan. What time window works?

If that aligns, I can drop a calendar invite and Connor will bring the preliminary perf expectations table.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0191

Thanks Markus — this lines up well with our internal notes. Quick answers:

- Peak: we see a sustained 700 rps during peak hours and occasional spikes to ~1.1k for 10–20 minute windows during marketing pushes.
- Typical short prompt: ~120 tokens in/out (mostly chat), heavy multimodal/long-doc jobs average ~6–9k tokens.
- SOC2 contact: I’ll loop in procurement and our security lead (separate email) — they’ll want the architecture whitepaper and a scoped evidence checklist.

We’d like to get a POC window scheduled for the last week of Sep if possible; procurement will need the scope/estimate to start the internal review. Could you include any expected cost ranges for a week-long POC in your follow-up?

Also — can you confirm whether KV cache persists between requests (for chat sessions) or is per-pod ephemeral in your POC topology? That matters for our session-based UX.

Best,
Eleanor

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: VirtuaSoft throughput & topology confirmation

Hi Eleanor — great, thanks for the numbers — that helps a lot. Short answers and next steps below.

KV cache behavior
- For the POC we’ll provision a persistent KV cache within the dedicated cluster (best-effort durability across pod restarts for session continuity). For production we can switch to the customer-managed VPC-backed cache + snapshotting for stronger durability guarantees.

POC sizing & cost estimate (rough)
- POC plan (7 days): 4x A100-80GB equiv reserved nodes with one autoscale node pool (up to 8 nodes) for spike validation. Estimated consumption: ~12,000 GPU-hours across the week (includes burst windows).
- Rough cost range (hosted + reserved infra + managed service): $45k–$65k for the week (final numbers depend on model variant and quantization options). We’ll provide a detailed breakout if you confirm the POC.

Proposed timeline
- This week: sign off on SOW scope (we’ll send a short SOW + MSA link).
- Sep 18–22: staging/POC execution (we can shift earlier if procurement moves faster).
- Week after POC: joint review and production readiness checklist.

Action items I’ll take today
- Share a short SOW + preliminary cost breakout (DocuSign link in related links).
- Connor will be on the deep-dive next Tue 09:00–10:00 PT; I’ll send an invite for Tue 09:00 PT — please tell us if Wed is preferable.

Would love a one-paragraph on procurement priorities so we can tailor the SOW (billing cadence, PO terms, security review lead).

Thanks — looping Connor for the deep-dive prep.

Best,
Markus
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
